identity.title: RL-GPT: Integrating Reinforcement Learning and Code-as-policy

problem.claim: The paper addresses embodied tasks requiring both code-based high-level planning and task-specific low-level refinement.

gap.claim: The authors identify limitations of LLM tool use for intricate logic and precise control, motivating integration with reinforcement learning.

contributions.claim: Introduces RL-GPT, a two-level hierarchical framework with slow and fast agents integrating coding and reinforcement learning.
Assigns the slow agent to analyze which actions suit coding and the fast agent to execute coding tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present RL-GPT as a seamless integration of code-as-policy and reinforcement learning through a two-agent hierarchy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that RL-GPT outperforms traditional RL methods and existing GPT agents, with superior efficiency.
The authors report that RL-GPT rapidly obtains diamonds in Minecraft within one day on an RTX3090.
The authors report SOTA performance across all designated MineDojo tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs can use tools by coding but are limited in intricate logic and precise control.
The abstract distinguishes code-suitable high-level planning from RL-suited low-level action refinement in embodied tasks.
RL-GPT integrates the modalities through slow and fast agents with separate analysis and execution roles.
The authors report efficiency advantages, stronger comparisons, rapid Minecraft diamond acquisition, and SOTA results on designated MineDojo tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps distinct task levels to distinct mechanisms and then assigns separate agents corresponding analytical and execution roles.

lessons.interpretation: This offers a precise way to explain why a hybrid system is structured as it is.
lessons.application: For a hybrid-method paper, explicitly align each task level with the mechanism and component responsible for it.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the task does not have a meaningful hierarchical split or when components cannot be assigned distinct roles.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative efficiency metrics, task counts, baseline configurations, or statistical details.
The scope and evaluation criteria of the designated MineDojo tasks and the meaning of SOTA are unspecified.
The reported one-day Minecraft result does not state the full experimental protocol or success criteria.
